newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens again.

text.p: The Australian bond yield curve continuedA last week's flattening trend, mirroring similar action in U.S. debt ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
The meeting is widely expected to endorse a 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates, a move that has now been largely factored in, traders said.

However, curve flattening phases, especially in response to any policy moves in the U.S., could present opportunities to exploit bear market steepening trades, according to Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

"The short end of the Australian curve is likely to be well protected with no increase in cash rates for many months to come. The long end, however, will periodically be vulnerable to both the local pro growth policy emphasis and higher yields from the United States," Roberts added.

Local bond yield spreads to the U.S. were fairly mixed on Monday, although the market was outpaced by Canadian bonds, which firmed on Friday after comments by Finance Minister Paul Martin and Bank of Canada governor Gordon Thiessen.
Thiessen said that there was room for strong growth in output and employment in coming quarters without impacting inflation, and he believed the Canadian dollar was in an upward track.
Martin, meanwhile, said he was confident that the Canadian economy could withstand a hike in U.S. rates.
